title: WhyNoIPv6 — Site Activity
description: Live view of what visitors are doing on the site, built entirely from check_job — the API's one user-driven write path (07-api.md §5.1). Operational counterpart to 'Public Engagement' (wni6-engagement), which holds the 30-day strategic view. NOTE: this is not a webserver dashboard — no nginx access-log telemetry is collected anywhere (09-ops.md §12 pins Grafana to read Postgres directly), so HTTP status codes and page-view counts are not available. check_job retention is 30 days (live_check.retention=720h), which bounds every range here.

panels.title: Checks
panels.description: Live checks requested in the selected range.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) AS checks FROM check_job WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at)

panels.title: Unique requesters
panels.description: Distinct requester IPs in range — the closest thing to a visitor count without webserver logs.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(DISTINCT requester_ip) AS requesters FROM check_job WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at)

panels.title: In queue now
panels.description: Jobs currently pending or processing. Ignores the time picker — this is a right-now gauge. A number that only grows means the crawler-side consumer is not draining.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) AS queued FROM check_job WHERE status IN ('pending', 'processing')

panels.title: Oldest in queue
panels.description: Age of the oldest un-completed job. Yellow at 5 min (live_check.reclaim_after — a lease should have been reclaimed by now); red at 15 min (live_check.fail_after — the reaper should have failed it).

targets.rawSql: SELECT coalesce(extract(epoch FROM now() - min(created_at)), 0) AS age FROM check_job WHERE status IN ('pending', 'processing')

panels.title: Failure rate
panels.description: Share of completed jobs in range that failed.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'failed')::float / nullif(count(*) FILTER (WHERE status IN ('done', 'failed')), 0) AS ratio FROM check_job WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at)

panels.title: p95 wait
panels.description: 95th-percentile wall time from request to result — what a visitor actually waits on the /check page.

targets.rawSql: SELECT percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY extract(epoch FROM completed_at - created_at)) AS p95 FROM check_job WHERE status = 'done' AND $__timeFilter(created_at)

panels.title: Check traffic by outcome
panels.description: Request volume over time, split by job outcome. The shape of site usage — bucket width follows the time picker.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroup(created_at, $__interval) AS time, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'done') AS done, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'failed') AS failed, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status IN ('pending', 'processing')) AS in_flight FROM check_job WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: What visitors are finding (base AAAA)
panels.description: Raw observation status of the apex AAAA across completed checks — the answer visitors actually got. Vocabulary is the live-check raw-observation set (07-api.md §5.1.4), not confirmed state.

targets.rawSql: SELECT coalesce(result->'checks'->'base'->>'status', 'unknown') AS outcome, count(*) AS checks FROM check_job WHERE status = 'done' AND $__timeFilter(created_at) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Latest live checks
panels.description: The 50 most recent checks, newest first — who asked about what, and what they got back. Deliberately NOT time-filtered: this is a live feed, so it always shows the newest activity regardless of the time picker. 'Wait' is request→result wall time; 'Scan' is the engine's own duration.

targets.rawSql: SELECT created_at AS "Requested", host AS "Domain", status::text AS "Job", coalesce(result->'checks'->'base'->>'status', '-') AS "Base AAAA", coalesce(result->'checks'->'www'->>'status', '-') AS "WWW AAAA", coalesce(result->'checks'->'mx'->>'status', '-') AS "MX", coalesce(result->'checks'->'ns'->>'status', '-') AS "NS", round(extract(epoch FROM completed_at - created_at)::numeric, 1) AS "Wait s", (result->>'duration_ms')::numeric AS "Scan ms", coalesce(error, '') AS "Error" FROM check_job ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 50

panels.title: Most-checked domains
panels.description: What visitors are looking up in the selected range. Repeat subjects are outreach candidates.

targets.rawSql: SELECT host AS "Domain", count(*) AS "Checks", count(DISTINCT requester_ip) AS "Requesters", max(created_at) AS "Last" FROM check_job WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC, 4 DESC LIMIT 25

panels.title: Top requesters
panels.description: Requester concentration, grouped the way the rate limiter groups it — IPv6 collapsed to its /64 prefix, IPv4 exact (07-api.md §6.3). One prefix dominating with few distinct domains is a bot; the per-prefix budget is live_check.rate_ip_per_hour (10/h).

targets.rawSql: SELECT CASE WHEN family(requester_ip) = 6 THEN set_masklen(requester_ip::cidr, 64)::text ELSE requester_ip::text END AS "Requester", count(*) AS "Checks", count(DISTINCT host) AS "Domains", max(created_at) AS "Last" FROM check_job WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 25

panels.title: Failure reasons
panels.description: Grouped error text for failed jobs in range. 'timed out' is the reaper (live_check.fail_after); anything else comes from the engine.

targets.rawSql: SELECT coalesce(error, '(no message)') AS "Error", count(*) AS "Jobs", max(created_at) AS "Last" FROM check_job WHERE status = 'failed' AND $__timeFilter(created_at) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 25

panels.title: Visitor wait time
panels.description: Median and p95 request→result wall time for completed checks. This is the page-load experience on /check, not engine performance.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroup(created_at, $__interval) AS time, percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY extract(epoch FROM completed_at - created_at)) AS p50, percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY extract(epoch FROM completed_at - created_at)) AS p95 FROM check_job WHERE status = 'done' AND $__timeFilter(created_at) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Hourly volume vs global rate cap
panels.description: Checks per clock hour against live_check.rate_global_per_hour (500). Touching the line means real visitors are being turned away with 429s — raise the cap or investigate the source in 'Top requesters'.

targets.rawSql: SELECT $__timeGroup(created_at, '1h') AS time, count(*) AS checks FROM check_job WHERE $__timeFilter(created_at) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
